One LinkedIn profile as one row: name, headline, location, About (500 chars), current company, school, followers, link. `profile` = the public identifier (williamhgates) or the linkedin.com/in/ URL; an internal id (ACoAA…) needs a session. The launches on Product Hunt's home page today, in the site's own rank order: name, tagline, the score on the vote button, the first topic and the product link. `limit` caps the rows. Columns: name, tagline, votes, topic, url.

Reddit's search results as posts: title, the post's page, what it links to, score, comment count, author, time, flair and the first 300 characters of the text. The posts of one subreddit: title, the post's page, what it links to, score, comment count, author, time, flair and the first 300 characters of the text. `sort` is hot, new, top or rising; `t` the window for top; `limit` up to 250 (100 posts per page). The remote jobs listed on Remote OK right now, from its public API: title, company, tags, location, salary range, date, the job's Remote OK link, the apply link and the first 300 characters of the description. `tag` keeps jobs with that tag (rust, design, …), `keyword` keeps jobs whose title, company or tags mention it; `limit` caps the rows. Papers on arXiv that match a query, from the arXiv API: title, authors, the first 500 characters of the abstract, the paper's page, the PDF, submission time and primary category. `sort` is relevance or date; `category` narrows to one arXiv category such as cs.LG; `limit` up to 100. The products a Shopify store lists at its public /products.json, one row per product: title, handle, product URL, vendor, product type, the lowest and the highest variant price as the store's own text (no currency code: the store's default currency), whether any variant is in stock, the variant count, the first image, the tags, and the update time. `store` is the store's host (allbirds.com) or its URL, with a market path (www.x.com/en-ca) when the store has one; `limit` is products per page (up to 250); `page` picks a later page. Questions on Stack Overflow with a tag, from the Stack Exchange API: title, link, score, answer count, views, whether an answer is accepted, time, tags, author, id and the first 300 characters of the question. `sort` is activity, votes, creation, hot, week or month; `limit` up to 100 in one call. Columns: title, url, score, answers, views, answered, created, tags, author, id, text.

post.summary: A Steam game's price, reviews and facts

One public company's profile from Yahoo Finance as one row: name, exchange, sector, industry, full-time employees, business summary, head office address, phone, website, the key officers with title, age and pay, Yahoo's five governance risk scores (1 low to 10 high) and the market cap. `symbol` is a Yahoo ticker (AAPL, 7203.T, SAP.DE) or a Yahoo Finance quote or profile URL. The reviews on a company's Trustpilot page, newest first, one row per review: star rating, title, full text, publish and experience dates, reviewer name, country and review count, verified flag, likes, the review's link and its language. `domain` is the company's site as Trustpilot names it (www.notion.so); `stars` asks Trustpilot for reviews with at least that rating (20 per page, also for a low-rated company); `page` reads a later page of 20. get.summary: Web search answer with sources and citations (research)
get.description: Answers a question or a whole agent prompt (up to 4,000 characters) from the web's current top results, with the pages it drew on. Ask for JSON in the question, or pass a JSON Schema, and the answer is JSON of that shape. answer.source says whether the text is Google's own answer (google_ai_mode, google_ai_overview) or written from the pages (crawl4ai). answered is false, and free, when the pages hold no answer. Experimental: fields may be added.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: the question or prompt, up to 4,000 characters; say the shape you want inside it, e.g. 'answer with JSON only: {...}'

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: a JSON Schema object as a JSON string, up to 4,000 bytes; the answer is then JSON of exactly that shape (parse answer.text)

parameters.name: deep
parameters.description: 1 reads pages and writes an answer when the web has none; 0 returns only the web's own direct answer, else answered false

parameters.name: gl
parameters.description: search country, e.g. us

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: search language, e.g. en

parameters.name: nocache
parameters.description: 1 skips every cache

post.summary: Extract structured data from a web page (contact, JSON)
post.description:
Scrape a page (crawled for you) or read your own content, and return typed JSON matching a JSON schema and/or a plain-English instruction, extracted by an LLM.

Send url or content, plus instruction and/or schema.

content.description: your own text, Markdown or HTML instead of a URL

examples: the top 3 stories on the front page

schema.description: JSON schema each returned record must match

example.description: a sample of the shape you want (structure, not values)

post.description: The items of any RSS 2.0 or Atom feed: title, link, publication time, author, the first 300 characters of the summary, and the item's id. Give the feed's `url`; `limit` caps the rows (up to 200). Columns: title, link, published, author, summary, id.

post.summary: List every URL of a site without crawling it
post.description: A site's URLs from the sources that already know them: its sitemaps, the links on its home page and the newest Common Crawl indexes (mode full adds the Wayback Machine). One call, 1 to 3 seconds for most sites. Each row: url, sources, last_seen, depth.

domain.description: the site's host; a leading https:// is dropped, www and the bare host are one site

mode.description: full adds the Wayback Machine, up to 20 s more

include.description: keep only matching URLs: a path prefix (/docs) or a glob with * over the path

post.summary: Scrape or read a web page as clean Markdown, HTML or PDF
post.description:
Scrape one URL, a web page or a PDF, into clean, LLM-ready Markdown text and/or HTML. Crawl4AI picks the cheapest engine that works (archive, plain fetch, real browser that renders JavaScript), with optional links, media, metadata and tables; proxies for sites that block datacenters.

Most pages answer in 1-2 s; a page that needs a real browser takes 10-30 s, and a failed page ends within about 55 s. A PDF URL returns the PDF's text as Markdown. Images and other binary files answer 422 binary-body within about a second, free. Blocked (403), unreachable (502) and fleet-busy (503) answers are free; retry a 503 after a few seconds.

proxy.description: Costs more: isp 0.30 credits, residential 0.60 (plain page 0.15). Use only for a site that blocked a plain request, and try isp before residential.

country.description: Two-letter exit country for isp or residential, e.g. us, gb. A country without isp addresses is served through residential at 0.60.

parse.description: true for all, or pick {links, media, metadata, tables}

For follow-up questions, related queries, an entity card, videos and news, use crawl4ai.web.search.rich.

post.description:
Search Keenable's web index with site, publication, acquisition and point-in-time filters.

Results include title, URL, description, snippet, and optional published/acquired timestamps. Unknown body fields are refused locally on the shared key.

mode.description: pro performs deeper retrieval; realtime returns faster. The response echoes the mode actually used.

acquired_after.description: RFC 3339 date, ISO 8601 timestamp, or relative delta such as 7d, 30min, 2h, 6mo, or 1y.

acquired_before.description: RFC 3339 date, ISO 8601 timestamp, or relative delta. A bare date includes that full UTC day.

published_after.description: RFC 3339 date, ISO 8601 timestamp, or relative delta.

published_before.description: RFC 3339 date, ISO 8601 timestamp, or relative delta. A bare date includes that full UTC day.

query_time.description: Search the index as it existed at this date or timestamp; relative filters are rebased to it.
